question.problem:
Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$

*Hint: You may wish to use the following identity: $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}.$*
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we recall the identity for $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2}):$

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}
$$

Therefore, using $x=\theta $ in the previous identity, the integral can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={2(-2)(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2}))|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-4(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-4(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-1) \\  & =4-2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
